text:
Alex K: Heads up — CI is red on my feature branch (feature/stacked-commits) after I merged main this morning. Failing cluster: kv_tests::test_kv_consistency + a bunch of timeouts.

ci-bot: Build #4312 queued for feature/stacked-commits (commit 9a7f2c). Logs: https://ci.redwood.example/build/4312

Maria P: @Alex K can you paste the failing test output? fast glance: is it a real failure or infra flake? :eyes:

Alex K: Pasted tail of failing job:
```
E       AssertionError: expected 42, got 0
E       File "tests/kv/test_consistency.py", line 78, in test_kv_consistency
E         assert value == expected
----------------------------- Captured stdout call -----------------------------
worker 1: timed out waiting for secondary to catch up
```
Looks like a replication timeout. Locally I ran the suite against main and it passed.

Tim L: Hm, we merged a db schema tweak in main yesterday that changed replication backoff. Could be an ordering/regression. Did you rebase or cherry-pick?

Alex K: I rebased main onto my branch and resolved conflicts. No schema changes in my commits. I can try a local bisect if people think it's necessary.

Sri R: Quick checklist: 1) Can you reproduce with `pytest -k kv --maxfail=1 -q`? 2) Try setting `REDWOOD_DB_REPLICA_TIMEOUT=30` locally to see if flakiness is just a timeout.

Alex K: Running `pytest -k kv --maxfail=1 -q` now. If it reproduces, I'll run git bisect.

Jordan M: If it's infra (worker timeouts), rerunning CI after clearing the cache sometimes helps. I can queue a rerun once you confirm it's not local.

Alex K: Quick local run: still passes. So maybe infra-only. But the CI logs show a different trace about the replication backoff code path (new main codepath).

Maria P: @Jordan M please hold off on rerun for 10m while Alex tries `REDWOOD_DB_REPLICA_TIMEOUT=30` and a targeted run. If it's flakey we can rerun and then escalate to eng-infra.

Alex K: Done — with env var set it passes locally. Without it, it's flaky. Looks like main tightened timeouts. I can either: 1) adjust my tests to tolerate the new timeout behavior, 2) file a follow-up to adjust the replication backoff, or 3) add a temporary test marker to skip on CI until infra patch lands. Thoughts?

Tim L: Option 1 is preferable if the behavior change is intentional. Can you open a small PR on your branch that updates the test to poll a bit more, with a comment referencing the main change? We'll review fast.

Alex K: Will do. I can push a tiny test tweak and then request a single rerun.

Jordan M: OK once you push I'll trigger a rerun and watch. If it still flaps, I'll escalate to eng-infra and schedule a quick bisect on main. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Build #4315 started (rerun requested by Jordan M)

Alex K: Pushed test tweak (commit 9a7f2d) and requested review @Maria P. Thanks everyone for quick triage.

Maria P: Reviewing now. If green, merge and we can follow up with a cleanup ticket for the timeout semantics.

Sri R: For the record, create an eval in infra-runbook so we can correlate recent main deploys with replication metrics next time.

Alex K: Will file ticket after merge. Closing loop here once CI is green.

Jordan M: Thanks — keeping this thread for the rerun trace.

Maria P: Looks good to me, approve.

ci-bot: Build #4315 succeeded (all checks passed)
